HISTORY, SUPERSEDED BY THE DESTRUCTOR FOLD (last boundary_evidence entry): THE DESTRUCTOR PAIR IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THE LICENSED RANGE, so the licensed run is 0x020b66a8..0x020b6814 (4 functions) inside the 0x020b660c..0x020b6814 object the evidence above establishes. The cartridge places _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD0Ev at 0x020b660c BELOW _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD1Ev at 0x020b6664. Measured here with mwccarm 2004/b56 on this TU, four source forms, one compile each, reading the object's .text section order: (1) default deferred codegen with the members in reverse-ROM source order emits [D1, D0, func_020b66a8, Render, Behavior, func_020b676c]; (2) `#pragma defer_codegen off` before the members emits [func_020b676c, Behavior, Render, func_020b66a8, D1, D0]; (3) the same pragma placed AFTER the members has no effect at all and reproduces (1) exactly; (4) the pragma plus the whole file rewritten in ROM-ASCENDING order emits [func_020b66a8, Render, Behavior, func_020b676c, D1, D0]. The pragma moves the pair between the head and the tail of the object and reverses the four real members, but the PAIR'S INTERNAL ORDER IS D1-THEN-D0 IN ALL FOUR. No arrangement of source text available to an inline-in-class destructor emits D0 first.

THE ONE FORM THAT WOULD EMIT D0 FIRST IS REFUTED BY THE CARTRIDGE. An out-of-line destructor definition emits D2, D0, D1 -- a D2 the ROM never carried -- and it is ruled out independently of that: the tree-wide relocation census finds _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD0Ev (0x020b660c) named by EXACTLY ONE word in the image, ov002:0x02109218, and _ZN16daObjKaitendai_cD1Ev (0x020b6664) by exactly one, ov002:0x02109214. Those two words are slots 17 and 16 of _ZTV16daObjKaitendai_c (address point 0x021091d4; 0x02109214 - 0x021091d4 = 0x40 = slot 16). No instruction anywhere in the ROM calls either destructor, and all five descendants inline this destructor's vptr store instead. An out-of-line definition here would make those five emit a `bl` the cartridge does not have and break their already-matched TUs. This is the same disposition already taken by ov002/daObjFloatBoard_c, whose destructor pair sits in the identical D0-below-D1 arrangement.

POST-PROMOTION `tubuild.py linkcheck` IS STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE TO THIS ENTRY, and that is not a defect in it. Once the single intact delinks.txt entry exists, linkcheck treats the source as an enrolled intact-object candidate and routes its object through tools/tu_production.prepare_intact_object, which refuses any entry that does not claim a non-text section: 'intact production requires one .text claim and at least one non-text claim'. This TU claims .text only, because the class has no factory, no g_profile row and no owned data. Control: running the same command against ov002/daObjFloatBoard_c -- long landed, promoted and byte-matched on main -- produces the identical refusal, so the message is a property of the command's intact path and not of either TU. The proof of record for this entry is therefore the pre-promotion scratch link below (scratch-link-verified, full ROM built and byte-identical to the stock control), which is the same state 33 other promoted text-only entries carry, plus tools/rombuild.py against the real tree. production_mode is deliberately left unset, as it is on 125 of the 132 promoted text-only entries.
